title: Beto to miss Everton’s trip to West Ham with concussion, says David Moyes
content:
David Moyes has confirmed that Beto will miss Saturday’s game against West Ham United due to concussion.

Beto, 28, has been in impressive form for Everton recently, scoring four goals in his last four Premier League games.

However, the Guinea-Bissau international was substituted in the second half of the 2-1 defeat to Liverpool last Sunday due to a head injury, and Everton manager Moyes confirmed that the striker would miss the game against West Ham United, along with defender Jarrad Branthwaite, who has been ruled out for the rest of the season with a hamstring injury.

“Beto has a concussion and will miss this week’s game,” Moyes told reporters on Friday. “Jarrad will be out for the season. Those are the two out at the moment.

“Jarrad is a bit better because he realised that it isn’t an injury to the same hamstring that he had an operation on. We hope that he gets back.

“It’s far from growing pains, but I think he is still learning a bit about himself. I hope that is the case, but he has had a couple of hamstring injuries, and we are obviously worried about it.”

Beto’s injury could see a return to the starting line-up for Thierno Barry. The 23-year-old striker, who joined Everton from Villarreal last summer in a deal worth an initial €32million (£27.5m), plus bonuses, hasn’t started a Premier League game since February 23.

The Athletic reported on March 15 that the Metropolitan Police had opened an investigation after reports of an altercation at the Emirates Stadium, which appeared to involve Barry’s friends after their 2-0 loss to Arsenal.

When asked what more the French striker can do to help the team, Moyes replied: “He can score, play well, and be a team player. We don’t ask for much more. We are just asking him to do the best he can possibly do.

“He’s had moments this season where he has been very good for us, and we are hoping that he can do that again if I choose to play him.”

Moyes was also asked about 18-year-old youth striker Braiden Graham. The Northern Ireland youth international has scored 21 goals in 31 games in youth competitions this season, and scored four goals and provided an assist in an 8-4 victory over Ipswich Town on April 17 for Everton Under-21s.

“I’m pleased that Braiden is doing really well,” Moyes said. “I think he has a bit to go before he is at the (first-team) level, but I’m really pleased. He might have more of a chance to get noticed during pre-season.”

Saturday sees Everton travel to face 17th-placed West Ham, a side Moyes took charge of 261 times across two spells, at the London Stadium.

When asked about his former club’s struggles this season, Moyes, who will take charge of his 750th Premier League game on Saturday, said: “It is a really good football club which certainly shouldn’t be going into the Championship, but the Premier League is unforgiving. If you are not quite at it, you don’t recruit right or don’t spend enough, then you could find yourself in that position every year.

“I’m really sad for the situation the club find themselves in. I hugely enjoyed my time in London. I had a brilliant time there with the players and the staff. I know what it means. If you get relegated, a lot of people are going to lose their jobs. I really hope that isn’t the situation.”
